subject: Order Form term mechanics — notice window alternatives & termination for convenience tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marc Delgado <marc.delgado@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Order form term questions — notice window + termination for convenience

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we review the draft Order Form: our legal team is pushing back on the auto-renew + 60-day notice language in section 3. They prefer either a 90-day notice or an option to convert to month-to-month after year one. Separately they want to limit termination for convenience to the customer only, or if mutual, to require a 6-month notice.

Can you share what flexibility Redwood can offer on notice windows and whether we can avoid an early termination fee? We're close on budget and timeline, but these term mechanics are blockers.

Thanks — happy to join a quick call if easier.

Jenna Ortiz
Procurement Lead, Acme Corp
jenna.ortiz@acme-corp.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marc Delgado <marc.delgado@acme-corp.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form term questions — notice window + termination for convenience

Jenna — thanks for the clarity. Appreciate the specifics from Acme Legal. High level: we can be flexible but need to balance predictability for Reserved capacity and the price bands tied to term length. A few concrete options for you to consider: 

- Option A (Standard): 1-yr term, auto-renew for successive 1-year periods, 60-day notice to opt out before renewal (current draft). No early termination fee except partial refunding of any committed reserved capacity on a prorated basis.

- Option B (Customer-friendly): 1-yr term + auto-renew, 90-day opt-out window. Termination for convenience (customer-only) permitted with 90 days' notice; no termination fee. Pricing would need a ~5% uplift on unit rates to compensate.

- Option C (Hybrid): 2-yr initial term with pricing discount; after year 1, customer may convert to month-to-month with a 90-day notice (effectively prevents immediate churn). Termination for convenience mutual with 180-day notice; early exit results in 3 months of committed minimum billing.

I've looped in Nikhil from legal to give redline guidance on language and on how we phrase the mutual termination mechanic to preserve our ability to recover committed costs. If you prefer, we can put Options B and C into the OrderForm and show the price delta.

Happy to set a 30-min call this week. Proposed times: Wed 5/19 10am PT or Thu 5/20 2pm PT.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
Attachments referenced: none
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Marc Delgado <marc.delgado@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form term questions — notice window + termination for convenience

Kimberly / Jenna — I took a pass at concrete redlines and attached a marked PDF (Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and a draft Order Form (OrderForm_DRAFT_5.docx) that encodes Options B and C with the corresponding price deltas. Highlights: 

- Wording for auto-renew: recommend keeping auto-renew but make the notice period configurable per Order Form. Suggested clause: "Customer may provide written notice to non-renew at least [X] days prior to the end of the then-current Term. If no notice is provided, the Term will automatically renew for the same duration."

- Termination for convenience: if Acme requires customer-only termination, we need to (a) attach a commitment schedule for reserved capacity or (b) include an early termination charge equal to remaining committed months at a mutually agreed rate. Alternative is mutual termination with a longer notice (180 days) and pro rata settlement of reserved spend.

- Month-to-month conversion: allowed after 12 months with 90 days' notice; require 3 months' minimum billing after conversion to manage capacity churn.

I've also suggested a short clause for transition assistance (30 days of migration support) and data export obligations in the event of termination.

Sending the redline as tracked — see attached. Let me know which option Acme prefers and we can finalize the Order Form and update pricing.

--
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf; OrderForm_DRAFT_5.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-21T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form term questions — notice window + termination for convenience

Team — quick decision from my side to keep momentum with Acme: authorize offering Option B (1-yr + 90-day opt-out, customer-only termination with no fee, ~5% price uplift) as a standard commercial concession for midmarket accounts. If Acme prefers Option C (2-yr + convert-to-m2m), escalate to me and product for a deeper review of capacity commitments.

Nikhil, please finalize the redline for Option B and create a version of the Order Form that shows the 5% uplift and the 90-day notice fields filled in. Kimberly, propose the two times and push the calendar invite once you hear back from Jenna.

Laura Bennett
